name: chaperonin containing TCP1 subunit 8

function.text: CCT8 is the approved symbol for chaperonin containing TCP1 subunit 8. Reviewed functional annotations implicate its product in ATP hydrolysis activity; ATP-dependent protein folding chaperone; positive regulation of protein localization to Cajal body.

germline.text: No conflict-free strong or definitive constitutional disease relationship met the source-selection criteria for this draft; this does not exclude a germline association.

somatic.text: Cancer Hotspots v1 reports recurrent residue-level observations in Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma; Low-grade glioma; Hepatocellular carcinoma. This is statistical recurrence evidence; it does not establish that every variant in this gene is a driver or a clinically actionable alteration. Evidence in this collection is restricted to the historical V1 release.

function.text: CCT8 encodes chaperonin containing TCP1 subunit 8. It forms part of the chaperonin-containing T-complex (TRiC), a molecular chaperone complex that assists the folding of actin, tubulin and other proteins upon ATP hydrolysis. The TRiC complex mediates the folding of WRAP53/TCAB1, thereby regulating telomere maintenance.

somatic.text: Somatic alterations involving CCT8 have been reported in low-grade glioma, prostate adenocarcinoma, and hepatocellular carcinoma.
